topic: Applications of Sets to Real-World Problems
title: 25 + 18 Is Not 43! Counting Sets Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Diya's class survey: 25 students like tea, 18 like coffee and 10 like both. Add 25 and 18 and you get 43, more students than there are. Nobody lied: the 10 who like both were counted twice. In this animated lesson we use sets to count real groups correctly. This is the topic of NCERT Chapter 1 (Sets) that the current rationalised NCERT text no longer includes, but JEE Main still asks it, so we teach it as a JEE problem-solving tool.

You will watch a live count of the class where the overlap lights up as counted twice, build n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B) step by step, compare "likes tea" with "likes only tea", check the answer with the three pieces of the Venn diagram, and solve a cricket and football problem that asks who plays neither. Then the exam trap of just adding, an original JEE Main pattern question on percentages with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students. Survey numbers in this video are example figures.

In this video:
0:00 25 like tea, 18 like coffee, 10 like both
0:30 The symbol n(A)
0:35 Live: count the class, catch the double count
0:58 The formula for n(A ∪ B), step by step
1:30 Likes tea vs likes only tea
2:03 Check with the three pieces
2:17 Worked example: cricket, football, neither
2:59 Exam trap: just adding
3:15 Where it is asked
3:25 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
3:57 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 13): Cartesian Products of Sets. Three snacks and two drinks in the canteen: how many different combos?

Video by Quest Academy.
